projects.name: dev-prune
projects.tagline: Gigabytes back. Nothing you can't rebuild.
projects.summary: A Rust CLI that reclaims the disk space idle repositories are holding in node_modules, .venv, target and vendor directories. It deletes one only after verifying read-only that the project's lockfile can rebuild it, and the same binary restores what it removed.

projects.name: CogniGate
projects.tagline: One endpoint in front of every model your applications use.
projects.summary: A self-hosted, multi-tenant LLM gateway: one key and the OpenAI API shape in front of every model your applications use. The edge gateway is Go 1.26 on Fiber v2, with provider plugins, analytics, and a conformance suite that runs in CI.

projects.name: LoginLens
projects.tagline: A local-only map of how you sign in to everything.
projects.summary: A browser extension that records which account, OAuth provider and MFA method you used on each site — the layer above passwords that nothing else tracks. It never asks for, reads or stores a password, and runs entirely on-device with no server and no account.

projects.name: Chronos-Ledger
projects.tagline: A multi-dimensional timetable engine, self-hosted and offline-first.
projects.summary: A multi-dimensional timetable engine, built campus-first for organization scheduling and attendance and generalizing to anything that needs to slice and query such a timetable efficiently. It replaces paper registers and spreadsheet timetables, runs entirely on an organization intranet with Docker as its only runtime dependency, and keeps working read-only, queueing writes, when the network drops.

projects.name: EquiLens
projects.tagline: Black-box bias detection for local language models.
projects.summary: A bias-auditing framework that probes any Ollama-compatible language model purely through its input/output interface, with no access to weights. It generates demographically paired prompts, runs them concurrently against a local model, and reports statistically analysed differences in the responses.

projects.name: Code-Ledger
projects.tagline: Your DSA grind, on your GitHub. Automatically.
projects.summary: A browser extension that commits every accepted competitive-programming solution to your own GitHub repository — code, problem statement and an optional AI review — with no extra steps after install. Practice that used to vanish into a judge's servers becomes a reviewable history.

projects.name: Facial-Emotion-Detector
projects.tagline: Facial emotion classification from landmark geometry.
projects.summary: A facial emotion recognition pipeline that detects faces, extracts MediaPipe landmarks, and classifies the expression from landmark geometry rather than raw pixels. It ships the full workflow — image collection, dataset preparation, training and inference — as scripted steps.

projects.name: SignLanguageDetector
projects.tagline: Sign language recognition, collection to browser inference.
projects.summary: An end-to-end sign language recognition project: collect images, build a dataset, train a classifier, and serve real-time predictions in the browser from webcam hand landmarks. It also exposes a headless REST endpoint and swaps trained models without a restart.

projects.name: PulseWard-HMS
projects.summary: Licensed proprietary software developed under a commercial licence. The repository is private, so this entry records the work rather than linking to public source — details available on request.

projects.name: Vectra-180
projects.tagline: A dual-fisheye dashcam for the Pi Compute Module 5.
projects.summary: A headless dashcam that records continuously from a dual-fisheye USB camera, protects the footage around an impact, and serves clips to a phone over Wi-Fi. Because the two lenses sit a fixed distance apart it can also compute a depth map — on request, never while a clip is being written.

projects.name: eVidya
projects.tagline: A JSON-defined learning platform that runs entirely in the browser.
projects.summary: An interactive tech learning platform with course content, YouTube video lessons, quizzes and progress tracking, built in vanilla JavaScript with no server and no database: courses are static data definitions and progress lives in localStorage. Adding a course means writing data, not code, and that JSON-first approach later shaped this portfolio's own settings-driven design.

projects.name: cspell-sync
projects.tagline: Your custom words. Everywhere. Automatically.
projects.summary: A VS Code extension that keeps cSpell custom words in sync between every project and the global dictionary, in both directions. Words added in one project reach the global list a second after the settings file is saved, so opening a new project no longer means red squiggles under your whole technical vocabulary.

projects.name: Eldritchify
projects.tagline: A cosmic-horror Zalgo generator: corrupt text, then purify it.
projects.summary: A Lovecraft-themed web tool that corrupts text with Unicode combining characters and cleanses it back. Adjustable chaos from 1 to 100, live preview, one-click copy, and a purification mode that strips the Zalgo marks out again, all served as an installable PWA on Cloudflare Pages. An actual weekend project, and a really fun one.

projects.name: RanobeGemini
projects.tagline: AI reading companion for web novels and fanfiction.
projects.summary: A local-first browser extension that improves the readability of machine-translated web novels, summarises long chapters in place, and tracks a reading library across several sites. It works with Gemini, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or a local Ollama model.

projects.name: ViewFlare
projects.tagline: Serverless view counter and SVG badges on Cloudflare.
projects.summary: A serverless telemetry counter for projects and documentation, built on Cloudflare Workers and D1 with a Hono API. One POST increments a project's views and one image URL renders a live SVG badge, so a repository gets usage counts without anyone running a backend. Formerly published as CFlair-Counter.

projects.name: the-pensive-index
projects.tagline: Discovery-first fanfiction search with prompt generation.
projects.summary: A fanfiction discovery platform designed to search existing tagged stories against complex, nuanced criteria before offering to generate a prompt. Tags are hierarchical with conditional branching rather than flat, so a search can express a specific premise instead of a keyword. In progress: the data and admin layers are built, the discovery search is not yet wired up.

projects.name: Youtube-Keystrokes-Blocker
projects.tagline: Toggle every YouTube hotkey individually.
projects.summary: Fine-grained control over YouTube keyboard shortcuts, as both a native browser extension for Chrome, Firefox and Edge and a userscript. Each of 30+ hotkeys can be toggled on its own, blocking suspends itself while you type in any input field, and settings persist through chrome.storage.sync or the userscript manager.

projects.name: ToxicGuard_AI
projects.tagline: On-device toxic language detection in the browser.
projects.summary: Toxic Shield is a cross-browser Manifest V3 extension that flags or censors toxic language as it is typed, using TensorFlow.js and the toxicity model. The content script forwards text to the extension's background service worker, which runs the classifier; the text being checked never leaves the browser.

projects.name: Save-Sync
projects.tagline: Save points for code, for when git is overkill.
projects.summary: A checkpoint tool for projects where full version control is more ceremony than the work deserves — experiments, tutorials and quick prototypes. A VS Code extension that snapshots the text of a workspace folder and writes it back on demand, so a risky change can be walked back without a branching model.

projects.name: ActionsCounter
projects.tagline: Project analytics on GitHub Actions alone — superseded by CFlair-Counter / ViewFlare.
projects.summary: An event counter with no server: a single GitHub Actions workflow, run on demand from the Actions tab or by a repository_dispatch webhook, keeps per-project counts in the repository's own Actions variables as base64-encoded JSON, and a Vite dashboard published to GitHub Pages reads them back. A PostgreSQL storage mode is also implemented. This is the earlier approach to the problem; the current counter is CFlair-Counter (being renamed ViewFlare), which runs on Cloudflare Pages/Workers with D1 and serves counter.vkrishna04.me. ActionsCounter stays online as a working record of the Actions-based design.

projects.name: BreachCheck
projects.tagline: Email and password breach lookup — Streamlit app and CLI
projects.summary: Checks whether an email address or password appears in known data breaches, from either a Streamlit web interface or a command-line interface. Password checks use Have I Been Pwned's k-anonymity range endpoint, so only a five-character SHA-1 prefix is sent and the suffix is matched locally. The two email lookups send the full address to the upstream service.

projects.name: docs-rag
projects.tagline: Retrieval-augmented QA that refuses to guess.
projects.summary: A retrieval-augmented question answering system over documents you choose — PDFs, Markdown, HTML, Wikipedia and GitHub files. It answers only from those documents, cites what it used, and refuses when they do not contain the answer, with that refusal verified mechanically rather than merely requested in the prompt.

projects.name: HiveXplore
projects.tagline: A Hive blockchain social client, built in 36 hours.
projects.summary: A hackathon build for IIT Delhi CodeHive: a social client that reads posts, profiles and wallet history straight off the Hive blockchain and broadcasts new posts back to it. It is here as evidence of working against a chain rather than as a product.

projects.name: portfolio-creator
projects.tagline: Fill in a form, get a portfolio.
projects.summary: A guided form that writes the one file a portfolio is configured by. It runs entirely in the browser with no backend and no account, validates every answer against the portfolio's own JSON Schema, and can create the repository and turn on Pages at the end.

projects.name: CareReach
projects.tagline: Telemedicine demo: symptom checks, hospital search, appointments.
projects.summary: An AI-powered telemedicine platform for remote healthcare consultations, built as a Streamlit app. Users chat with Gemini 1.5 Flash about their symptoms, search nearby hospitals by specialist type through the Google Maps Places API, book appointments, and review their health history, with bcrypt-hashed logins stored in SQLite.

projects.name: EchoSight
projects.tagline: Call QA reports from raw transcripts, with every flag auditable.
projects.summary: A contact-center call quality review tool that turns a raw transcript into an annotated coaching report in a single API call. Deterministic, rule-based moment detection keeps every flag auditable, Gemini powers transcript simulation and a live interactive agent chat, and the in-memory store sits behind a small adapter so it can swap to any database without touching business logic. Built for a hackathon and complete as delivered.
